# presetdiff.py v1 (2026-09-10) | old=C:\Dev\SMR-SrcArchive\1.0.7.396349\Src digest=09d95e3448573dc3… | new=C:\Dev\SMR-SrcArchive\1.1.0.403908\Src digest=a4577da25cb3fe85… | python presetdiff.py --out docs/agent/reports/vanillahunt | 2026-09-10
# SCOPE: the `generated` bucket only — Data/, Lua/BuildingTemplate/, Lua/XDef/, Lua/ClassDefs/. DLC/ excluded.

# PRESETS: 1.0.7=14409  1.1.0=14986. Identity is `class::id::group` (how the GAME names a preset), with id-less presets keyed `class::file#ordinal`. Matched presets whose FILE moved: 0. Ambiguous ids needing a disambiguator: 1.0.7=1 1.1.0=0.

# ⭐ ROUTED TO 02, NOT READ HERE: the tech registry exists TWICE in 1.1.0 — 264 `TechPreset` in 1.0.7 became 274 `TechPreset` PLUS 441 `Tech`, and 258 of the 1.0.7 ids appear under both classes in the new tree. Mechanical count only; what it means is a reader's question.

# ⛔ REORDER IS NOT A ROW, BY CONSTRUCTION: rows are keyed by key PATH, so re-emitting a preset's keys in another order with equal values yields nothing. 0 presets are in exactly that state — COUNTED here so that `no rows` and `never looked` do not look alike.

# ROWS BY CHURN CLASS: COMMENT=1  REINDEX=10462  REINDEX-SWAP=1924  T-ID=22  added-preset=1471  none=22738  removed-preset=894   ⭐ `none` is the READABLE PILE — the rows 04's registry agents actually read.

# ⭐ THE GENERATED-LUA TWINS, so 04 can confirm they carry nothing extra: 1.1.0 files parsed per registry — Data=2191, Lua/BuildingTemplate=292, Lua/ClassDefs=7, Lua/XDef=426 | 1.0.7 — Data=2143, Lua/BuildingTemplate=288, Lua/ClassDefs=9, Lua/XDef=400

# ⚠️ CHURN CLASSES ARE CLAIMS. Each is a rule asserting a row is uninteresting; `python tools/presetdiff.py --sample <class>` prints rows so one can be falsified. A single row where a rule hid a real value change VOIDS that class.

# 02 COLUMNS: prid = P + 1-based data-row index of PRESETS.tsv. system = preset:<class>; link = 03 (dlc-adjacent) | 04-E (the registry agent) | NOT-READ(churn) for REINDEX / T-ID / COMMENT (rule-classed and sampled by 01, unread here — TRIAGE.md §4). ⭐ READ by a registry agent: `none` + `REINDEX-SWAP` (01: must be read where order is semantic) + `added-preset` + `removed-preset` (real content, not churn).

# 02 DLC TAG on presets: T1 literal on class:id + key + both values; T2 narrowed on id + key + values ONLY — never on the class name (a registry is not a mention). Literal matching of all 25 terms would tag 8,209 readable rows (all of TechPreset and LawDef by class name).

# 02 FIELD-REPORT TAGS (README §2b), column `fr`: FR-1(c) = `none`/`added-preset` rows of ParticleSystemPreset, LightmodelPreset, ActionFX*, *Entity* registries (assets first spawned at new game); FR-2 = id/key/value naming DeepScan / UndergroundDeepScanning / Deep* resources / depth_layer.

column6: T(803650464265, "Asteroids are separate areas that can be visited by Rockets and Asteroid Lander. There are different types of Asteroids, each with their own types and amounts of resources available on them. Asteroids are the only source of Exotic Minerals, but can also contain Metals, Rare Metals, Polymers, and Water. Mining these resources requires specialized extractors that require a specific tech for mining in Micro-G gravity. Asteroids can be discovered by Recon Centers and stay available until they are abandoned through the Planetary View or through the Asteroid icons at the bottom left of the screen. Be careful - all buildings, vehicles and resources present when abandoning an Asteroid are lost! Initially, only a single Asteroid can be tracked but with upgrades to the Recon center (some require a specific tech) this number can be increased up to three Asteroids at the same time. The available Asteroids can be viewed in the Planetary View or in the bottom left of the screen.")

column6: T(5373, "The Martian Colony is made up of a variety of buildings which provide power, life-support, comfort, protection from the weather, information, resources and a lot more - all things without which humans cannot exist on the Red Planet. Buildings are built by using resources and some can be brought from Earth as prefabs. Most buildings require a resource upkeep for maintenance. A construction site must be within the Service Area of Drones in order to receive the resources needed and then be erected. Some buildings require Power to operate, others are staffed by Colonists living nearby. The Performance of any building indicates how effectively the building is performing its primary function. It depends on many factors, such as researched technologies, upgrades and the current individual performance of the specific colonists working in the building. Qualified specialists and workers with high Morale will increase the performance of a building, while empty work slots, Renegades and workers with low Morale or other issues will be detrimental. Most buildings can be set to operate in three Work Shifts - first, second and night. Turning off some Work Shifts will conserve power and workforce.")

column6: T(12180, "Martian surface temperatures are freezing at best while being extremely cold most of the time. Although humans can't withstand the Martian cold outside Domes (not without protective gear anyway), most of our machinery is designed to function effortlessly in the cold. This, however, is subject to change when a weather event known as a Cold Wave appears. The low-density Martian atmosphere allows for rapid and dramatic temperature drops - drops so low that all field buildings have to spend increased amounts of electrical power to keep from succumbing to the cold. During a cold wave, all Water Towers freeze solid, rendering the colony somewhat vulnerable to water shortages if more unfortunate events overlap. Out-dome buildings left without power also run the risk of freezing until the cold wave subsides or the area is heated via a Subsurface Heater. Buildings that have inactive shifts are very likely to freeze as well. Cold waves appear with a short warning period and also may be a seasonal event in areas of Mars flagged as being especially cold.")

column6: T(5417, "Every Colonist is a unique individual defined by his or her name, age group, workplace specialization, traits, and stats. Colonists will automatically inhabit Residences within their Dome. Take care to provide enough living space for all of them. Children and senior Colonists cannot work, but still require sustenance and residential space. The rest of the Colonists will seek jobs in and around their Domes, according to the building priority and their individual work specialization. Buildings with higher priority will be staffed first. Specialized Colonists will prefer to work in buildings corresponding to their individual specializations and will have better Performance at such workplaces. Traits define details about the individual Colonists. Traits that provide beneficial effects are called Perks, while Traits with negative effects are called Flaws. Quirks are neither positive nor negative. Rare traits define truly exceptional individuals. Every Colonist has four stats defining his or her current condition: Health represents physical fitness. Sanity represents mental wellbeing. Comfort represents the quality of the Colonist's life on Mars. Morale represents happiness, optimism and loyalty. For details about individual stats and a more comprehensive description of their effects, refer to the Colonist's Info Panel. Be careful - if all Colonists die, the Mars colonization mission will be terminated!")

Morale represents happiness, optimism, and loyalty. Colonists with high Morale perform better at work, while low Morale can turn them into Renegades. Colonists can improve their Stats through Services provided by buildings in the Dome they inhabit as well as buildings in connected Domes. Be careful - if all Colonists die, the Mars colonization mission will be terminated!")

column6: T(8118, "Colonists with no specialization may be educated to receive a specialization in the Martian University. The University can provide needed specializations automatically or focus on a single desired specialization. Some, but not all, undesirable Flaws may be cured in the Sanatorium Spire. Up to three different Flaws can be treated in a single Sanatorium. The School building cultivates desired Perks in children living in the Colony. They have a chance to receive any of the three selected Perks when they grow up. Not all Perks can be trained in Schools. The Playground building cultivates random Perks in children who visited it. The University, Sanatorium and School buildings are treated as workplaces - Colonists being educated or treated there cannot work a job at the same time. The individual Performance of the Colonists determines how fast they receive a specialization, cure a Flaw, or their chance to cultivate a Perk from School. The Playground service building grants its effect to any children who visit it at least once during their childhood.")

Up to three different Flaws can be treated in a single Sanatorium. The School building cultivates desired Perks in children living in the Colony. They have a chance to receive any of the three selected Perks when they grow up. Not all Perks can be trained in Schools. The Playground building cultivates random Perks in children who visited it. The University, Sanatorium and School buildings are treated as workplaces - Colonists being educated or treated there cannot work a job at the same time. The individual Performance of the Colonists determines how fast they receive a specialization, cure a Flaw, or their chance to cultivate a Perk from School. The Playground service building grants its effect to any children who visit it at least once during their childhood.")

column6: T(5419, "Colonists may migrate to new Domes within walking distance of their current position, or farther away when Train or Shuttle transport becomes available. Colonists can move to Underground Domes as long as they can reach the Dome - meaning they have to be able to access an Elevator from the surface and the Dome must be reachable from the Elevator in the Underground. Homeless Colonists will travel to another accessible Dome with available residential space. Each Dome can be set up to filter Colonists by age, specialization and other Traits. Colonists with ANY of the must-include traits, or ANY of the desired traits and NONE of the undesired ones will remain in the Dome. Others will seek another Dome with available living space and filter that matches their Traits.")

T(5397, "Drones are the backbone of the Martian colony's work force. They are tasked with distributing resources, gathering resources from surface deposits, building and maintaining structures, as well as repairing damaged structures and vehicles. Although mostly autonomous, drones operate within the Service Area of whatever controller they are assigned to, such as Drone Hubs, Rockets or RC Commanders. Drones run on batteries and need to charge up frequently. They may do so only at an RC Commander and Charging Stations which in turn can be built individually or are found attached to Drone Hubs.
All the heavy lifting and most of the field tasks are left to drones. They are powerful, semi-autonomous utility vehicles which are equipped with state of the art instruments fit for a wide range of manual labor. Built to be resilient against most of what the Martian environment can throw at them, the arch-enemy of all man-made technology on Mars - dust - will eventually incapacitate drones if not cleaned regularly.")

column6: T(5408, "All buildings deteriorate over time. When a building's maintenance bar is filled, a Drone is dispatched to bring the required maintenance resource and service the building. If the resource is not supplied within a Sol, the building will stop operating until maintenance can be performed. Martian dust and disasters contribute to the deterioration of buildings outside of Domes. Extractors, Martian dust geysers, Rocket landings and launches spread dust in the area around them, causing increased maintenance to nearby buildings. Drones are also susceptible to dust, which may result in a breakdown. Recharge Stations clean Drones during the charging process.")

column6: T(5376, "Mars is infamous for its large and sometimes quite lengthy Dust Storms, which raise so much dust that they can be seen with telescopes from Earth. While the wind speeds reached during these storms are not quite dangerous, taking into consideration that Mars's atmosphere is but 1% of Earth's, the sheer amount of dust raised can knock field machinery out of order until fixed. Another issue is that Mars's fine dust particles are extremely dry and slightly electrostatic, which can cause damage to our power grid if a dust storm with more electrostatic properties appears. MOXIEs and Moisture Vaporators do not function during dust storms and Solar Panels outside domes are closed automatically. Dust storms suspend air traffic - all Shuttles will finish their final courses and then return to their hubs until the storm passes. Electrostatic Dust Storms are a rare occurrence. Lightning strikes during such storms can shut down buildings for a time or drain the batteries of our drones. The greater the risk the dust storm is flagged to pose in an area, the higher the chance is for an electrostatic dust storm to appear. Dust storms can also be a seasonal event, happening routinely in the most high risk areas.")

T(760602736588, "Exotic Minerals cannot be found on Mars itself - they can be obtained by going on mining missions to Asteroids that are within range of Mars. Exotic minerals are mainly used to construct reinforced buildings that can withstand the harsh environments of the Martian Underground and asteroids.
One thing that both Mars and Earth have in common is that they lack certain mineral compositions that are beneficial to the development of our colony. It has long been known that there are asteroids rich in these exotic minerals, however, accessing them from Earth has always been problematic. Luckily, Mars is much better suited as a base for these mining operations, allowing us to gain access to resources and technology that were out of practical reach before.")

column6: T(5423, "The map is divided in Sectors which need to be scanned to reveal what resources and Anomalies they hold - if any. Sectors can be queued for scanning from the Map Overview. T(5384, "Food is grown on Farms and Hydroponic Farms, which are placed inside Domes, and also in Fungal Farms placed outside of Domes. Ranches are another option for food production. Farms and Hydroponic Farms can grow different crops with different cycle patterns. Furthermore, some crops, like algae, also generate oxygen for the dome they are grown in.
Making the Martian soil fit for farming, even within the protection of domes, takes heavy alterations. First, toxin removers are applied to rid the Martian regolith of toxic substances like perchlorates. Then, the use of chemical decompressors to break down common Martian compounds and make nutrients out of them is employed. And finally, specifically designed bacteria to further modify all nutrients made into a more plant-use friendly form, is introduced. Growing food on Mars greatly decreases costs and dependency on Earth.")
column7:
T(5384, "Food can be grown on Mars in a variety of buildings that offer different options for optimizing and customizing your colony. Hydroponic Farms and Farms can grow different crops with different cycle patterns. Furthermore, some crops, like algae, also generate oxygen for the dome they are grown in. Open Farms offer large-scale farming options, but are dependent on terraforming. Ranches are another option for food production and come in two variants - an in-dome ranch and an outside one. Fungal Farms are placed outside of domes in the Underground.
Making the Martian soil fit for farming, even within the protection of domes, takes heavy alterations. And finally, specifically designed bacteria to further modify all nutrients made into a more plant-use friendly form, is introduced. Growing food on Mars greatly decreases costs and dependency on Earth. Food is perishable and decays by each Sol.")

column6: T(625960246815, "Sustaining plant life on Mars is one of the major points of its terraforming. The spreading of vegetation on the surface of the planet requires Seeds to be imported from Earth, or grown on special crops in the Farms and Hydroponic Farms. The Seeds are then planted by Forestation Plants, or spread in the lower atmosphere by Rockets. Initially, the quality of the local soil is barely capable to sustain a bunch of lichen species, but as the lichen grow and spread, the Soil Quality will be improved. More complex plants, like grass, bushes and trees require increased local Soil Quality, higher Temperature and more Water on the planet in order to grow and spread. Bushes and trees yield Seeds, which can be harvested by Drones. Recurring Rains improve Soil Quality, while Toxic Rains decrease it.")

column6: T(5416, "The Founders are the first human pioneers of the red frontier and the first residents of the fledgling Colony. Their initial task is to prove the potential of the Colony and the viability of a permanent settlement on Mars. After the Founders arrive on the planet, the Colony will be under evaluation for a certain number of Sols. No new Colonists will be available until the Colony is evaluated positively. A positive evaluation will be awarded if any Founders survive a certain number of Sols, or if the first child is born on the Red Planet. Since the Founders number is limited to the capacity of the Rocket, you may wish to handpick them using the Filters on the Passenger Rocket screen. Take care to micromanage their tasks during their first days on the Red Planet, using building priorities and work slot management to guarantee that crucial buildings are staffed.")

column6: T(5413, "Colonists need Life Support resources in order to survive - Water, Oxygen and Food. Without access to any of these, a Dome will die out, with a shortage of Oxygen being the deadliest. Both Oxygen and Water are supplied to Domes via a Pipe Network, which must be connected to Oxygen and Water production buildings. Construct and connect Water and Oxygen Tanks to manage temporary shortages. Pipes are built by Drones and deteriorate during Dust Storms or could take damage from Meteors and Dust Devils, resulting in Pipe Leaks, which drain Water and Oxygen from the system. Drones repair Pipe Leaks at the cost of Metals. If a Dome is left without Power, it won't provide heating to Colonists and they may die due to exposure to the intense cold of the Red Planet. Food, which can initially be brought from Earth via Rockets, can be grown later on using Farms, Hydroponic Farms, Fungal Farms, and Ranches. In contrast to Water and Oxygen, Food is not a grid resource and needs to be transported with Drones.")

T(5387, "Machine Parts are manufactured in Machine Parts Factories from Metals and are mainly used in the construction and maintenance of the sophisticated resource extractors on Mars.
Back on Earth, we humans are dependent on machines to sustain our advanced way of life; to power our industries and make possible our vast transportation systems. Here on Mars machines are also tasked with making life possible to begin with, on top of potentially maintaining all of their previous obligations. Smart design processes and accepted standards have made possible the stockpiling of machine parts that could be used in an array of instruments upon demand. Machine parts can be delivered from Earth to meet the needs of any fledgling colony. But a hefty and reliable supply, one obtained only by having them manufactured on site, will be the foundation to bringing our Earthly way of life to the Martian dream city.")

T(5388, "Metal is readily found on the Martian surface, deposited from ancient tectonic activity and meteor blasts. Further deposits can be found beneath the surface (by either Orbital Probes or Sensor Towers) which can be then mined with Metal Extractors. Metal is a basic building material and is used in a wide range of buildings. It is also used for manufacturing Machine Parts.
Since very early in human history, metals have played a vital role in the art of creation. From simple copper tools and nails, to iron decorations and entire structures made out of steel. It would seem their role is not exhausted only on Earth, but will continue to serve as an accessible and vital resource for all our needs on Mars as well.")

Oxygen is the most short-term life support resource. If colonists are left without oxygen, they will die extremely fast. And while Mars's atmosphere has little to no oxygen, what it does provide is an abundance of carbon dioxide, which our brilliant MOXIE technology can convert to the much needed oxygen. Like water, it is supplied and distributed via pipe networks; in fact, sharing the same pipes used for water distribution.")

column6: T(5412, "Power is distributed among all buildings in the power network, which consists of Power Producers (and/or Power Accumulators) and all Power Consumer buildings connected via Power Cables or being adjacent to each other. Power Switches can be constructed along Cables, allowing you to connect or disconnect entire sectors of the grid at will. Power Cables can sustain Cable Faults (either from Meteors and Dust Devils, or during Dust Storms) and will need to be repaired every now and then by Drones - provided there are Drones within reach. Cable Faults drain power from the grid. Repairing them requires Metals and may take some time. IMPORTANT: Denser power grids develop more Cable Faults.")

T(10506, "RC Constructors are remote-controlled vehicles which can pick up and carry resources from and to various storage units across the surface of Mars. They can set up transport routes and maintain the flow of resources between two points on the map. Another function of these rovers is to gather resources from surface deposits of Metals and Polymers. The unique feature of the RC Constructors is the ability to construct buildings on their own without the assistance of Drones. They can utilize the resources carried on board and when the required amount of resources is delivered to the construction site, they can autonomously finish the building process.
The agenda of the Indian Colonization Program was to win the space race by doing what they do best - building their own path to victory. The RC Constructor was especially designed with that purpose in mind, to allow the resourceful Commander to quickly develop a growing Colony, setting up robust facilities and freeing valuable drone time.")

T(10507, "RC Drillers are unique remote-controlled vehicles developed by the Russian Colonization Program. Where similar rovers have a sizeable cargo hold for resource storage, the RC Driller sports an in-built driller probe with a single purpose - to exploit underground Metals or Rare Metals deposits. Thus, it has been completely stripped of its functions as a transporter. While extracting resources from underground deposits, the rovers waste 50% of the production, but, on the other hand, grant access to otherwise hard to get resources without the need of extractors and Colonist workforce. The usual rules for accessing an underground deposit apply - the relevant technology will be required to exploit Deep Deposits.
The Russian technology has proven reliable and robust, developed around one simple purpose - get the job done. The RC Driller makes no difference, and while it has some flaws, it provides an invaluable option to the ambitious Commander - the ability to rely less on the topography of the Red Planet and the presence of surface Metals deposits.")

T(5414, "New technologies will unlock new buildings, upgrades, Colonist perks and other benefits for the Colony. Standard technologies are divided in five fields with different themes. Researching any technology will make a new technology within its field available for research. Some technologies have fixed positions in their fields, others have randomized positions. Individual technologies are researched by generating Research Points (RP) equal to their costs. The Mission Sponsor may provide a fixed amount of RP per Sol, but research buildings will be needed to discover the later, more advanced, technologies in a timely manner. Outsourcing research is another option, granting a fixed amount of RP for a certain period in exchange for Funding. Analyzing Anomalies with an RC Explorer vehicle may grant RP or make new technologies available for research.
Breakthroughs are extraordinary technologies with powerful effects that are discovered only by special means. One way to unlock a Breakthrough technology is to discover it in an Anomaly on the surface of Mars. Different Breakthrough technologies may appear in each playthrough.")
column7:
T(5414, "New technologies unlock buildings, upgrades, Colonist perks and other benefits for the Colony. Technologies are organized into interconnected clusters, which in turn belong to broader fields. Each technology is linked to adjacent technologies, forming a network of possible research paths. Researching a technology will unlock any connected technologies, which may belong to the same cluster or extend into different clusters and fields.
All technologies cost 1 Tech Point to research. Tech Points are generated by accumulating Research and their cost increases every several Tech Points. The Mission Sponsor may provide a steady income of Research per Sol, but dedicated research buildings are essential to sustain scientific progress. Research can also be outsourced for Funding, temporarily boosting its generation. Certain discoveries and events can improve research efficiency. Anomalies, special events, or sponsor bonuses may grant a Research Boost, contributing a percentage of the Research required for the next Tech Point . Analyzing Anomalies with an RC Explorer may also unlock new technologies directly or provide additional research opportunities.
Breakthroughs are extraordinary technologies with powerful effects that cannot be accessed through normal research progression. They are discovered only through special circumstances, such as exploration or unique events, and vary between playthroughs.")

column6:
T(5396, "Rockets are used to deliver supplies all the way from Earth, or bring colonists which have applied for a life on Mars. They are reusable and, once having refueled on Mars, can export Rare Metals to Earth for monetary gains.
Space rockets have a far greater role to play in the mission of establishing a permanent colony on Mars than merely bringing the first colonists there. Until the colony can truly sustain itself, it will always be dependent on Earth for vital resources and the flow of colonists. Although quite expensive, reusable rocket technology has already been mastered to a degree that can have a rocket back in space within the same day of landing on either world. ")

column6: T(416603082686, "The Atmosphere parameter represents the density and the composition of the Martian atmosphere. The higher this parameter is, the more Earth-like the atmospheric pressure, oxygen levels and cloud generation will be. Atmosphere is increased by the Magnetic Field Generator and Carbonate Processor buildings and also by completing the Import Greenhouse Gases Special Project. Due to the lack of a planetary magnetic field, Atmosphere is gradually lost over time. Atmosphere improvement boosts the effectiveness of Wind Turbines and MOXIEs, but makes Solar Panels less productive. Recurring Dust Storms and Meteor Storms decrease in severity with the improving of the Atmosphere and later disappear entirely. In tandem with the Temperature parameter, when both parameters are high enough, the atmosphere on Mars becomes breathable and Domes may become open-air Domes.")

column6: T(629055319176, "The surface of Mars and the Underground are two independent maps that each have their own set of resources, vehicles, colonists and prefabs. They can be used to move vehicles, resources, colonists and prefabs between the two maps. \n\nBy using the Transport Cargo action on the Elevator, cargo can be selected that will be transported to the other side of the Elevator. Elevators function as a connection between these two maps. They can be used to move vehicles, resources, colonists and prefabs between the two maps. The Elevator functions as a storage for resources that is shared between the Surface and the Underground. T(7753, "The planet turned out to be even more hostile and uninviting than we thought, thwarting any attempts to make a breakthrough in its exploration.

T(5748, "The Cold Wave that had gripped our Colony has finally been dispelled. Temperatures have returned to the normal, cruelly cold levels we are used to.

Our scientists are confident that we have recorded and gathered all data necessary for making sense of this encounter in the coming decades. Also, they are confident that the Spheres themselves had overstayed their welcome. 

Keeping them around would have meant living with the ever-present danger of re-activating the endless Cold Wave once more, even if we had managed to find a way to halt it without destroying all the Spheres. 

And despite the risks, despite the purely pragmatic reasons for destroying all the Spheres, one can't help but wonder how the generations to come will feel of this deed. Will we go down in history as cowards? Or maybe as too insensitive to the magnitude of the encounter, the very first non-man-made technology ever found?

When our scientists give up on trying to determine the origin of these Spheres, will textbooks mention that because of the rash actions and fears of the few pioneers that lived on Mars at the time, the riddle will never be solved?

<effect> No more Spheres are left.
<effect> Cold Wave dispelled.")

Show once keeps it from appearing again in the same game and Log entry prefixes the text with a Mission Control log header.

column6: T(9464, "One by one, the Alien Crystals perished under our rule. We perceived them as mere resources, as milestones on our path to master the Universe. Only until we have finally gathered all the pieces we were able to see the puzzle and understand the wrongness of our actions. The crystals weren't singular entities but rather the different organs of an intelligent, thinking alien being.\n\nFor millennia the creature traveled through the vast expanse of space in its primal form - a swarm of meteor-like crystals. It fell on Mars and began its cocoon period, forming the outer shell of its parts from the fine dust and absorbing the bleak solar radiation. column6: T(8346, "People all around the world celebrate, but the consequences of the Wildfire crisis remain. We have decades - maybe even centuries before us - to cope with the damages caused, with the fear and desperation which reverberate inside all of us. But we remain optimistic that, given time, people will return to their everyday lives. The Wildfire crisis has shown us how fragile we are, how the ivory towers we've built could crumble in mere days. Maybe it's the perfect moment to step back and reconsider the way we lived our lives.
